memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the Lord your God will deliver them over to you, throwing them into great confusion until they are destroyed. He will give their kings into your hand, and you will wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will be able to stand up against you; you will destroy them. - Deut 7:23-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice who does the real work in these verses. It is the Lord who "will deliver them over," the Lord who throws the enemy into confusion, the Lord who gives their kings into Israel's hand. Yes, Israel would fight, but the victory belonged to God. Their part was to trust and obey; God's part was to secure the outcome. They would not win by their own strength but by the power of the God who fought for them.

This is a pattern that runs all through Scripture, and it corrects a mistake we easily make. We often approach our battles as though everything depends on us — as if our willpower, our effort, our cleverness must carry the day. But the deepest victories in the Christian life are won by God's power, not ours. Our calling is faithful obedience; the results rest in His hands.

This truth brings both humility and confidence. Humility, because we cannot boast — the victory is God's, not ours. Confidence, because our success does not finally depend on our fragile strength but on His unshakable power. "Thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Cor 15:57). The greatest victory of all — over sin and death — was won entirely by Christ, not by us. So face your battles today doing your part faithfully, but resting in the truth that the outcome belongs to the Lord who fights for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I approach my battles as if everything depends on me?
- How does knowing "victory belongs to the Lord" bring both humility and confidence?
- Where do I need to do my part faithfully while trusting God for the outcome?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, so often I fight my battles as though everything rests on me. Remind me that the victory belongs to You. Help me to obey faithfully and to rest in Your power, giving thanks for the victory You have won in Christ. Amen.
